## Why
The [current finding contract](https://github.com/grove/gapline/blob/main/gapline-audit/SKILL.md) already requires precise evidence, counterevidence, uncertainty, and the smallest useful next action. In practice, the final action could still be too vague for a developer to confirm or dismiss the concern. We should improve **actionability**, not simply add report fields.

**Evidence gate:** look at real-host and independently reviewed findings from [#4](https://github.com/grove/gapline/issues/4) and [#5](https://github.com/grove/gapline/issues/5) to identify examples where a more discriminating follow-up would reduce developer work.

## Proposed approach
- For each sufficiently consequential **SUPPORTED** finding or **HYPOTHESIS**, propose the smallest observation or controlled experiment that can distinguish the concern from plausible counterevidence, where meaningful and safe to describe.
- Specify relevant setup/trigger, expected and alternative outcomes, observable signal, assumptions, and scope **when these matter**. Do not force a rigid form for straightforward source/document contradictions, no-finding reports, or unknown contracts.
- Distinguish proposed checks from performed tests: executable tasks remain **PROPOSED — NOT RUN**. An audit itself remains read-only and must not silently call tests, builds, external services, or sibling projects.
- Preserve authoritative source of requirements and full observable contract (identity, ordering, side effects, exact bytes where relevant). Do not assert a reproduction from source-only reasoning.
- Compare old and new finding examples with independent reviewers: is the next action clearer, cheaper, falsifiable, and less likely to send the developer in the wrong direction?

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Include contrasting examples: actionable uncertainty, direct documentation contradiction, legitimate alternative, and insufficient requirement context.
- [ ] Follow-up tasks include a discriminating observation where possible, plus an explicit **NOT RUN** label for executable experiments.
- [ ] Independent review finds improved or equal actionability without misleading certainty or unacceptable verbosity/cost; report negative results.
- [ ] Keep the default report short (up to three findings) and avoid mandatory new schema or workflow steps.
- [ ] Revise the shipped skill/reference and evaluation cases only after documenting the expected improvement.

## Out of scope
Running probes, generating patches, opening issues automatically, or mandatory Proofline/Faultline integration.

## Field finding -> verification handoff examples from pg-trickle (2026-10-17)

The two Gapline runs on [pg-trickle @ `066bd5dcdfca`](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/commit/066bd5dcdfca8ad9ee3de9cf012a52d2774ba5dc) returned six source-based findings with counterevidence and a **smallest next verification step**. Follow-up triage expanded these into separate GitHub issues. **No pg-trickle reproduction or tests were run** in either original audit or in the subsequent source spot-check.

| Finding | What the first Gapline report already supplied | What made the follow-up more falsifiable |
|---|---|---|
| [G1 / #1158](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1158) | Two writers (A uncommitted before refresh, B later committed), verify two DIFFERENTIAL cycles | Witness **LSN and transaction ordering**, inspect persisted frontier/history, compare **exact** results after A commits, and prohibit a hidden FULL self-repair |
| [G2 / #1159](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1159) | RECEIVED WAL receipt, fallback to triggers, restart, check replay | Separate **durable-receipt-not-applied** from **WAL not yet decoded**; retain committed-input journal and slot/receipt identity; distinguish replay once vs explicit rebaseline |
| [G3 / #1160](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1160) | A→B COUNT graph, FULL/reinit then DIFFERENTIAL, verify parity | Record tick bound, upstream ST-buffer LSN, B's stored frontier and effective modes; require **next DIFFERENTIAL with no new source change**; identify graph-bound or transaction-order counterexample |
| [A1 / #1161](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1161) | Time-dependent expiration with no source writes and scheduled refresh | Observe **whether any tick is dispatched**, distinguish duration vs controller interval, compare live defining query before manual FULL, resolve **intended time-freshness contract** |
| [A2 / #1162](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1162) | Source/doc contradiction about `FOR KEY SHARE`, auto-downgrade and counter | The documentation mismatch can be corrected from source; a **separate, optional witnessed lock-timeout** test is needed only to assert actual runtime error/rollback |
| [A3 / #1163](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1163) | Source/doc contradiction: recursive CTEs support multiple DIFFERENTIAL strategies | Treat manifest + source + contradictory matrix text as enough for a **documentation fix**; optional strategy test must separate recursive-result recomputation from whole-table FULL |

**Product lesson:** The useful unit is a *discriminating observation*, not a test-list quota. For concurrency, name the exact interleaving, oracle, forbidden hidden repair, and alternate explanation. For time-based behavior, identify ambiguity in the public contract **before** declaring a defect. For direct docs contradictions, do not require a heavy integration test before updating demonstrably stale text. All suggested executable checks remain **PROPOSED — NOT RUN**; source-level `DEMONSTRATED` is not runtime-demonstrated behavior.

**Unproven benefit:** The extra reproduction detail came from subsequent triage, not a controlled A/B finding-format evaluation. No independent developer has yet reported that the refined handoff saved time; these are concrete examples to compare with old-format findings, **not proof** that longer reports are better.

**Candidate acceptance test:** have independent reviewers compare anonymized original-versus-refined handoffs on these cases, scoring whether each describes an executable discriminating test, alternative outcomes, correct source contract, and less avoidable developer effort. Include A2/A3 as controls against over-specification. Preserve the default 3-finding limit and short report.

title: [P1] Make consequential Gapline findings verification-ready
